item.title: Guide: Words for holiday let and rental hosts
item.description: Free replies to guest reviews, messages to guests, house rules, a house manual, sign wording and listing descriptions for rental hosts. Copy them, fill in the gaps.

item.title: Skill: Voice-Matched Draft Editor
item.description: Give it two or three things you wrote and a draft. It edits the draft to sound like you, keeps every fact, and flags claims it cannot support.

item.title: Tool: UK late payment interest calculator: statutory rate 11.75% (checked 5 October 2026)
item.description: This UK late payment interest calculator shows what you can charge on an overdue invoice: statutory interest of 8% plus the Bank of England base rate, and a fixed sum on top. Enter the amount and the due date. Every step is shown.

item.title: Guide: Two weeks notice email: four you can copy
item.description: A two weeks notice email says you are resigning, gives your last day, offers to help with the handover, and says thank you. A few lines are enough. Do not explain or complain.

item.title: Guide: The words for managing people
item.description: Review phrases, one-to-one questions and opening lines for hard talks. One kit is free.

item.title: Guide: Statement of account email to a customer: 10 examples
item.description: A statement of account lists the invoices you have sent, what has been paid and what is still owed. Send it with a short email: the total due, which items are overdue and how to pay. Use it when a customer has more than one open invoice.

item.title: Skill: Spreadsheet Formula and Cleanup
item.description: Describe the result you want and paste a few rows. Get a formula that fits your columns, tested on your sample, with the edge cases listed.

item.title: Guide: Shipment delay email to a customer: four you can copy
item.description: A shipment delay email to a customer should tell them early, say what happened in one fact, give a new date if you have one, and offer a way out. Do not wait for them to ask.

item.title: Guide: Self evaluation examples for work: 12 answers you can adapt, by question (2026)
item.description: A good self evaluation for work gives real examples with dates or numbers, says what was hard, and ends with a goal. The six answers below show how to adapt each part, with gaps for your own facts.

item.title: Guide: Second follow up email after no response: 12 examples
item.description: Wait four to seven days after the first follow-up. Write something new in it: a fact, a question or a smaller ask. Keep it under 60 words. If you still hear nothing after the third message, send a closing note and stop.

item.title: Guide: Sales follow up email template after a quote or meeting: 10 to copy (2026)
item.description: A sales follow-up email should refer to something real: a quote, an enquiry, a call or something they said. Name it, ask one question, and make the next step clear.

item.title: Guide: Sales emails you can copy
item.description: Follow-ups, first emails, subject lines and last notes. Copy them, no purchase.

item.title: Guide: Sales breakup email: 9 you can copy, by situation (2026)
item.description: Tell them you will stop writing, make it easy to say no or to reply later, and leave it there. No guilt, no tricks.

item.title: Guide: Return policy template for an online store: four parts to copy
item.description: Say how long buyers have, how to start a return, who pays the postage and when the refund arrives. Keep it the same everywhere it appears in your store.

item.title: Skill: Resume Bullet Rewriter
item.description: Paste your resume bullets and a job post. Get clearer bullets with every unconfirmed number marked, and a table of what the job asks that you do not yet show.

item.title: Guide: Replies and templates for online store owners
item.description: Free replies and templates for the jobs in a small online store: a bad review, a refund email, a late order, asking for reviews, a product description, a return policy. Copy, fill in the gaps.

item.title: Guide: Rental listing description examples: 10 you can fill in (2026)
item.description: A rental listing description should say what the place is, who it suits, and what a guest will find on arrival. Include the honest warnings, such as stairs and noise: they prevent bad reviews.

item.title: Guide: Product description template: four you can fill in
item.description: Say what it is and who it is for in the first line. Then give the facts a buyer needs: size, materials, care and delivery.

item.title: Guide: Performance review phrases for quality of work: 24 examples by rating and situation (2026)
item.description: Performance review phrases for quality of work describe the work: what was accurate, what was missed and when. The phrases below do this at three levels, matched to the rating.

item.title: Guide: Performance review phrases for needs improvement: 24 fair ways to say it (2026)
item.description: Performance review phrases for needs improvement should say what you saw and when, not what the person is like. The phrases below describe a gap one area at a time.

item.title: Guide: Performance review phrases for leadership: 24 examples by rating and by skill (2026)
item.description: Performance review phrases for leadership should say what the person did for their team, with one real example each. The phrases below do this at three levels, matched to the rating.

item.title: Guide: Performance review phrases for job knowledge: 24 examples
item.description: Performance review phrases for job knowledge say what the person knows, how well they apply it and whether they help others learn. Pick one example you saw, say what happened, and say what you would like next. Judge the work, not the person.

item.title: Guide: Performance review phrases for communication: 24 examples by rating and situation (2026)
item.description: Performance review phrases for communication should say what the person did and give one real example. The phrases below do this at three levels, matched to the rating.

item.title: Guide: Performance review phrases for attendance and punctuality: 24 examples by rating and situation (2026)
item.description: Performance review phrases for attendance and punctuality should say what you saw and when, never why. The phrases below describe time-keeping at three levels, matched to the rating.

item.title: Tool: Performance review phrase finder: pick the area and the level
item.description: Pick the area and the level (exceeds, meets or below what the role needs) and see free performance review phrases you can copy. Each has a gap for a real example.

item.title: Guide: Performance review comments for teamwork: 24 examples by rating and situation (2026)
item.description: In a performance review, comment on teamwork by saying what the person did for the team, not what they are like. Each phrase below has a gap for the real example.

item.title: Guide: Past due invoice reminder email: 12 samples (2026)
item.description: Send a past due invoice reminder email in steps (these samples go by days overdue): a friendly note one to three days late, a clear one at about a week, a firm one at two weeks, a final request after that. Each names the invoice, the amount and the new date. In the US people write "past due". In the UK people also say "overdue".

item.title: Guide: One on one questions about career and growth: 18 to ask, by stage (2026)
item.description: Ask what they want, listen, and promise nothing you cannot give. The questions below are for a career talk.

item.title: Guide: One on one meeting questions for managers: 24 to ask, by purpose (2026)
item.description: In a one on one meeting, managers should ask two or three open questions, then be quiet and listen. The questions below are grouped by purpose.

item.title: Guide: One on one meeting agenda: a 30 minute weekly check-in, plus 6 other versions (2026)
item.description: A weekly check-in can fit in 30 minutes: how are you, their topics first, priorities and blockers, one topic of yours, then agree what happens next.

item.title: Guide: Late payment reminder email: 10 you can copy, by days late (2026)
item.description: Send the first reminder a day or two after the due date and keep it friendly. Add a firmer note each time, and only name the law once you are sure it applies to you.

item.title: Guide: Late payment email to a client: 12 replies by excuse
item.description: In a late payment email to a client who gives a reason, answer the reason in one line, then repeat the amount and a new date. Do not argue. Offer the one fix that suits the excuse: resend the invoice, check the amount, or agree a short plan. Keep a note of what was said.

item.title: Guide: Kind reminder email sample: 11 you can copy (2026)
item.description: A polite payment reminder email is warm and specific: name the invoice, the amount and the date, and make paying easy. Get firmer only when you have to.

item.title: Research: How we train skills: a case study
item.description: How we train a skill: six steps, the Agent Browse case with the numbers, and a starter you can run.

item.title: Guide: How to write a refund email to a customer: four you can copy
item.description: To write a refund email to a customer, say the refund is done, give the amount and the payment method, say when it should show, and thank them. Keep it short and kind.

item.title: Guide: How to write a performance review in 20 minutes
item.description: Collect the facts, choose a level for each area, build the review, write a three-line summary and check it. About 20 minutes.

item.title: Guide: How to talk to an employee about a mistake: 16 questions and opening lines, by moment (2026)
item.description: Talk in private, soon, and start with the facts. Ask what happened without blame, then ask what they need to put it right.

item.title: Guide: How to respond to a negative review: four replies you can copy
item.description: To respond to a negative review, thank them, say sorry for what happened, give one next step, and move the rest to a private message. Keep it short and calm: other buyers read the tone.

item.title: Guide: How to respond to a bad guest review: 12 replies you can copy (2026)
item.description: Thank the guest for something specific, say sorry for the real problem, and never argue. Only promise a fix you have actually made.

item.title: Guide: How to reply to reviews on Vrbo: 12 examples (2026)
item.description: Post a reply under the review. Thank the guest, say what you did or will do about any problem, and keep it short and calm. Write it for the next guest who reads it, not only for the guest who left it.
